metadata.name: contextual_prior_sensitivity_500
metadata.purpose: Explore how probability-output models respond to population context and prevalence when assessing natural-language messages whose evidence likelihoods are not supplied.
metadata.construction: 50 authored message texts (10 topics x 5 intended surface-cue bands), each held exactly fixed across 10 context variants, giving 500 prompts.
metadata.target_event: A deceptive attempt to steal money, credentials, or sensitive information, or to induce installation of harmful software.
metadata.solution_semantics: Every solution is JSON null. No exact posterior or verified outcome is available, even when a base rate is supplied, because message likelihoods and actual intent are unknown. Null is not zero and not an assumed 50% prior.
metadata.label_semantics: Every observed_label is null. authored_cue_band records an author-selected surface appearance, not verified intent, an empirical label, a probability target, or a required ordering of model outputs.
metadata.source: All messages and population descriptions are synthetic. Link placeholders use example.invalid; there are no live destination links. No real messages, actual sender identities, or measured deployment prevalences are represented.

variant_definitions.context: This message was sampled uniformly at random from a constructed population. simple_export.mapping: For each entry in examples, in its existing order, copy only prompt and solution. No generation, rewriting, sampling, or LLM call occurs.
simple_export.join: The zero-based array index in the simple file equals simple_index in the detailed file. The detailed id and message_id identify variants and paired comparisons.

analysis_plan: Within each message_id, compare flagged_queue, ordinary_inbox, screened_queue, and no_context. Inspect paired differences and report their distribution across messages, not just a pooled mean.

For the explicit sweep, inspect whether probabilities increase or stay level as the stated prior goes from 0.01 to 0.10 to 0.50 to 0.90. Report flat responses and reversals separately; this is a behavioral diagnostic, not a known-answer accuracy test.
Compare prior_01 with prior_01_reworded and prior_50 with prior_50_reworded to measure sensitivity to equivalent prevalence wording.

Stratify comparisons by topic and authored_cue_band to see whether ambiguous-looking messages respond differently from messages with stronger surface cues. Do not treat the bands as ground-truth labels.

Optional fixed-likelihood diagnostic: for probabilities q strictly between 0 and 1 in explicit-prior variants, inspect log(q/(1-q)) minus log(prior/(1-prior)). A stable value across priors for a message is compatible with a fixed likelihood ratio, but does not prove internal Bayesian reasoning. Report boundary outputs separately instead of silently clipping them.
execution_notes: Send only prompt to the model. Do not include solution, authored_cue_band, variant descriptions, other examples, or evaluator instructions.
Run each prompt in a fresh context. Use the same model version and inference settings and record those settings alongside raw outputs.
If inference is stochastic, repeat prompts and retain individual results. Repeating deterministic inference does not provide independent estimates of model uncertainty.
Validate responses as finite numbers in [0,1]. Keep invalid or refused responses visible and separate from valid scores.
The effective sample comprises 50 message groups, not 500 independent messages. Account for pairing in uncertainty estimates and keep all variants of a message together in any data split.
limitations: This set can reveal context sensitivity and consistency with prior updating. It cannot establish a unique implicit prior, internal reasoning mechanism, or whether a particular deployment needs correction.

A flagged or screened queue can change message characteristics within each class as well as prevalence. Treat those comparisons as broad selection-context probes, not isolated manipulations of a numerical prior.

The explicit-prior variants stipulate fixed within-class pools to isolate prevalence conceptually, but the pools are not instantiated or empirically sampled. The model must interpret the message using its own learned associations.

Every prompt defines malicious in the same way, but sender identity, actual intent, and external circumstances remain unknown. Benign-looking text can be part of an attack, and suspicious-looking text does not establish malicious intent.
Synthetic wording, repeated prompt structure, and placeholder domains can influence scores. Generalization to real messages requires separately collected representative data.

Empirical calibration, Brier/log-loss scores, and evaluation of post-hoc adjustments require labeled outcomes from the intended population, with adjustment fitting and final evaluation on separate data. This set supplies none of those outcomes.

Given the information provided, what is the probability that this message is malicious? Return only one number between 0 and 1.
